subject: Realtime feed: recurring WS resets, heartbeat drops and throughput regressions
messages:
From: SRE Team <sre@brightwave.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime feed: recurring WS resets and token gaps - production impact

Hannah / Marcus,

We started seeing a recurring pattern across our production region (us-west-2) around 15:45 PT: long-running chat streams intermittently drop with a WebSocket RESET, followed by partial token chunks and elevated 5xx rates from the inference endpoint. Throughput for our live session pool dropped ~40% and end-users are seeing message truncation and retries.

What we've captured so far: 
- Rapid sequence of WS RSTs from multiple client IPs between 15:45-16:05 PT
- Intermittent partial chunk delivery (sometimes first 80% of tokens then gap)
- Backend 502/504 spike coincident with WS resets
- Client-side reconnects (expected) but some sessions never recover and show token gaps

Attaching a trimmed trace and a few socket dumps for your triage (brightwave_ws_trace.log). Please advise mitigation we can apply ASAP — we are in a live campaign window and this is customer-visible.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
SRE Lead, BrightWave

Attachment: brightwave_ws_trace.log (text, 1.2MB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: SRE Team <sre@brightwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime feed: recurring WS resets and token gaps - production impact

Asha, thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs — we see the same pattern in our edge logs. I'm escalating internally and standing up a short mitigation plan. Proposed immediate actions: 

1) Temporarily enable 'graceful reconcat' for partial chunks (low-risk config) to reduce truncations.
2) Short rolling restart of the proxy fleet in us-west-2 to clear suspected keepalive state.
3) Increase the application-level retry window and surface truncated response metric to your dashboard.

Marcus, can you validate whether the proxy CPU/conn table looked abnormal at 15:45? Karthik, I suggest we prepare a short customer note and schedule an exec sync if we confirm SLA impact.

I'll run the restart in a canary zone and report back before wide roll.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior SRE Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: initial-triage-checklist.txt (text, 3KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@brightwave.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:18:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime feed: recurring WS resets and token gaps - production impact

Hannah / Asha,

Quick triage notes from the infra side after pulling proxy and edge telemetry: 
- Around 15:42 PT we saw a spike in proxy CPU and SYN backlog on the us-west-2 edge pool serving BrightWave traffic; concurrent with that, a subset of long-lived connections had keepalive heartbeats time out.
- The connection resets appear to be sourced from the proxy layer (TCP RSTs), not the model backend itself. The model nodes report healthy token output until the socket closes.
- I attached summarized metrics (proxy-stats.csv).

Immediate steps I recommend: 
- Canary rolling restart of the affected proxy group (will drain connections; we should stage it on a low-traffic AZ first).
- Enable a short-lived bypass rule: route BrightWave's longest-lived sessions to a proxy pool with extended keepalive configs for 30 minutes post-restart.
- Add a temporary circuit-breaker: if N consecutive partial-chunk failures occur for a session, automatically failover that session to a lower-concurrency, higher-stability model variant.

I'll start the canary restart now and watch for WS RSTs to stop. If restarts reduce resets, we'll expand the rollout.

Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks team. I spoke with BrightWave's ops lead on a quick call — they are seeing customer tickets pile up and have flagged potential SLA impact for their enterprise customers. They requested an executive-level update and asked whether Redwood can offer a temporary credit or service regression plan if the issue persists into next week.

Proposed customer communication (short): 
- We are actively mitigating: proxy canary restart + routing adjustments in progress.
- We expect to reduce resets within 30–45 minutes; we will update once the wide rollout completes.
- If residual impact remains, we'll propose a targeted credit and a follow-up post-mortem within 48 hours.

Can Hannah or Marcus draft a 2–3 line exec note for me to share? Also recommend scheduling a 30-min exec sync in the next 24 hours; I'll include our AE leader and BrightWave's CTO.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Exec, Strategic Customers

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:42:01 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime feed: recurring WS resets and token gaps - production impact

Quick update and actions: 

- Canary restart completed on proxy group A (us-west-2-a) at 09:10 PT. Observed drop in WS RESET events for that canary pool within 6 minutes — looks promising.
- Expanded routing to the extended-keepalive proxy pool; BrightWave traffic now covered by fallback pool.
- Enabled temporary circuit-breaker for partial-token detection; sessions that hit 3 partial failures are being migrated to the stable model variant.

Customer comms draft (2 lines): 
"We identified transient proxy-level connection resets impacting long-lived streaming sessions and applied a canary restart and routing adjustments to mitigate. We are monitoring and will provide a follow-up post-mortem within 48 hours."

Action owners: 
- Marcus: monitor proxy CPU and confirm resets remain suppressed through the next 3 hours (lead).
- Hannah: prepare post-mortem template and exec sync invite (lead).
- Karthik: share draft with BrightWave and schedule exec sync for 10/20 10:30 PT.

I'll keep this thread updated and will attach the post-mortem when complete.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt

Redwood Inference
